What's New

Recent features and improvements

14-Nov-2026

The Core Is Fair Source — The public core is licensed under the Functional Source License: read it, run it, change it and use it inside your organisation. Each release becomes Apache 2.0 open source two years after it ships. The enterprise package adds the OBDA planes, identity federation, key managers, branding, the prompt editor and signing.

12-Nov-2026

Ready Sooner, With an Expert Included — The server answers within seconds of starting while the embedding model loads in the background, and a new installation comes with the Uderia Expert agent already installed and its documentation already indexed.

11-Nov-2026

Your Licence at a Glance — The Info box shows the licence this deployment runs on: its tier, which parts of the enterprise package it covers, who holds it and when it expires.

02-Nov-2026

Agents That Ask Instead of Guess — When an agent cannot go on without you — two things with the same name, a value nobody recorded, a step that needs your go — it stops and asks. The question appears as a card under the answer; your answer continues the turn. It holds in scheduled runs, flows and across coordinated agents, and a Needs Input view shows everything waiting on you.

01-Nov-2026

Agents That Use Uderia Itself — An agent can find and call the platform's own operations as you, scoped by the roles you give it (Guide, Agent Builder, Knowledge Curator, Automation Builder, Quality Analyst, Insight Builder, Publisher, Admin Monitor, Problem Solver); a change waits for your approval where it must.

31-Oct-2026

Agents Can Ask Other Agents — Where an administrator allows it, an agent asks the agents its owner lists — a route, a second opinion, what is missing — and each answers in a conversation of its own, recording who asked.

31-Oct-2026

Counts You Can Trust — The platform counts for the model, so 44 agents are reported as 44; and when a data source is unreachable the answer names the data source, never the model provider.

30-Oct-2026

A Clearer Assurance Guide — Each control now shows the properties it assesses, the modules it uses during the turn, and only the measures that really share its code. Every S points to its M; click either letter to see the other.

30-Oct-2026

See What Decided the Grounding Gate — The gate states the finding it acted on, such as "1 of 13 statements unmatched — annotated", marks the modules it consulted, and shows what each one read.

29-Oct-2026

Follow-Up Questions Understood Again — Every agent type now receives the conversation's earlier answers, so a follow-up is answered in context instead of repeating the first answer. Turn Summaries mode (the Alt key) applies to every agent type.

29-Oct-2026

An Honest Answer When the AI Provider Fails — If the model provider fails (no credits, a rejected key, an outage), the answer says so in one plain sentence, the turn is recorded as failed, and the quality score shows it.

29-Oct-2026

Lower Cost Through Prompt Caching — Optimize planning reuses its cached prompt with Claude (direct, through OpenRouter or on Bedrock), Amazon Nova, OpenAI, Azure and xAI.

29-Oct-2026

Each Agent Learns on Its Own — New Optimize agents learn into their own planner repository, so one agent's lessons never steer another. Existing agents can opt in.

28-Oct-2026

Every Model Has a Price — Each model in use is priced automatically or named as unpriced, and spend is booked under the model that was actually called, judges included.

26-Oct-2026

The Right Tools for Each Question — Relevant per turn now finds tools by meaning as well as by words; the setting lives with each agent under Data sources → Tools.

26-Oct-2026

Safe Editing in Two Tabs — An open canvas, flow or dashboard follows changes made in another tab without overwriting your unsaved work.

25-Oct-2026

Better on iPad — No more zooming into text fields, the keyboard no longer covers the composer, and the page can't be dragged out of place.

24-Oct-2026

Manage Your Files From Components — Components → Files now has a Files tab to search, rename, keep, download, delete and restore your files, like the tabs for canvases, dashboards and flows. Changes made in another tab or through the API appear at once.

24-Oct-2026

Files in Your Cloud, Under Your Keys — Keep files in Azure Blob Storage or Google Cloud Storage as well as a folder or S3, and wrap their keys with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS or HashiCorp Vault — each tested before it is used.

24-Oct-2026

Ask About a Spreadsheet — Attach a CSV, TSV or Excel file to a question and the agent reads it as a table. The Files panel shows where a file was used as the turn starts, and reopens when you return to the conversation.

24-Oct-2026

Save Any Export to Files — Every download — a receipt, a graph, a canvas file, an audit pack — can be kept in Files in one click, and a dashboard becomes a PDF snapshot with each tile's refresh time.

24-Oct-2026

Agents and Flows That Work With Files — Let an agent find, read and save files itself, let a flow read a kept table and keep its results, and add a kept document to a knowledge repository.

24-Oct-2026

Keep What Your Conversations Produce — Keep any table, chart or answer in one click, then find it again from any conversation, see where it came from, and ask a new question about it.

24-Oct-2026

Files You Can Govern — Admins choose where files live — a local folder, a network share or S3 — encrypt them by default, set each tier’s space and downloads, and every download is recorded.

23-Oct-2026

An Assurance Guide in Plain Words — Every check is explained in one layout, in words the screen defines, and the Guide opens at the check you clicked — from the Trust Circle or from an answer.

22-Oct-2026

Figures That Mean What They Say — The agent, trust and awareness tiles now count exactly what their labels promise, with one definition of a failed turn and one time window throughout.

20-Oct-2026

A Trust Circle That Reads at a Glance — The ring opens with a one-sentence verdict, a chosen watch-only setting reads calm instead of alarming, and every station says what it checks.

20-Oct-2026

Smooth Typing Beside Large Graphs — The question box stays instant while a large knowledge graph is open beside the conversation; a hidden loop that kept the page busy is gone.

20-Oct-2026

Clear When You Are Signed Out — When a session ends, the page says so once and offers to sign in again, instead of every panel quietly showing an empty list.

15-Oct-2026

Panels That Stay Current — A change made anywhere — another tab, the agent editor or a script calling the API — appears in every open panel without reloading the page.

14-Oct-2026

Answers, Not SQL — When a model writes a query instead of running it, the platform runs it safely and answers; a record that no query produced is flagged.

14-Oct-2026

Token Counts You Can Trust — Streamed responses are counted once, and a turn on another agent records the model that actually served it, so costs match the provider’s bill.

14-Oct-2026

Signatures That Survive a Sync — When a synced knowledge repository changes, your standing policy decides whether its signature carries forward, renews, or waits for you to review it.

14-Oct-2026

Proven Answers Replay Instantly — Ask a question that a signed example already answers, word for word, and the proven answer comes back without spending a single token.

13-Oct-2026

Governed Data as Components — Signed data products, model authoring and actions are now components you switch on per agent, each with one policy: off, observe or enforce.

12-Oct-2026

Design an Action Step by Step — Define an action in the Actions Designer: choose the connection and the concept, and the platform derives the checks it must pass before it can be signed.

12-Oct-2026

A Faster Start — Sign-in, the agent anatomy and the trust pages open without waiting on slow lookups or external libraries, even on large estates.

09-Oct-2026

Ready for Regulated Use — A hardened mode tightens sign-in, keys, idle sessions and audit for regulated deployments, and refuses to start until every key is properly secured.

09-Oct-2026

Every Answer Shows What It Was Made With — Open an answer’s trust record to see each part that produced it — agent, ontology, skills, model, data — whether it was signed then, and whether it has changed since.

09-Oct-2026

Evidence Anyone Can Check — Export one answer or your whole estate as a single file and verify it offline, in a browser or with a small script, with no Uderia server involved.

07-Oct-2026

Agents That Change Records, Safely — Agents can update records through signed action contracts: every write is checked in one transaction, sealed with a receipt, and can be undone.

07-Oct-2026

Four Eyes on Every Write — Name a supervisor for an agent, and its writes wait for that person’s approval. The owner cannot approve their own agent’s writes.

07-Oct-2026

Act From Flows, Schedules and Dashboards — A signed action can run as a flow step, on a schedule, or again from a pinned dashboard tile, always under its own rules.

07-Oct-2026

Faster Queries, Proposed for You — The platform studies the queries your agents ran and proposes statistics or indexes. A person approves, and the gain is measured.

07-Oct-2026

One Model, Two Warehouses — A model extension can be deployed to PostgreSQL as well as Teradata, each to its own design standard, and read back to prove it.

06-Oct-2026

Grow the Model From a Question — When the model lacks a concept a question needs, the agent proposes it. You review the draft, then land it on the warehouse.

05-Oct-2026

Sharper Knowledge Graph Context — The graph brings in only what the question reaches, and follow-up questions keep the entities the conversation was about.

04-Oct-2026

A Calmer Question Box — The question box shows progress while the agent works and a receipt afterwards: verdict, time, tokens and cost.

04-Oct-2026

Answers Read Cleanly — Formatting in answers renders properly, and platform notes are clearly marked as the platform’s, never mistaken for the agent’s words.

03-Oct-2026

Create From the Workspace — Every Workspace section that can create something now has a “+”, and you can drag panels into the order you work in.

02-Oct-2026

Flows From a Shape — Pick a pattern such as pipeline, debate or pair programming, and the flow is built and staffed for you. Loops stop once a judge is satisfied.

02-Oct-2026

See Why a Query Is Slow — Explain any query and see its plan as a graph of steps, with costly patterns flagged first. Change it, explain again, and see what improved.

02-Oct-2026

Upgrades Back Up First — An update that changes the database layout takes a backup before it starts, and refuses to start if it cannot.

01-Oct-2026

Proven Teradata SQL Patterns — A library of Teradata SQL patterns, every statement run on a real Teradata before it ships. Agents open only what their own database can run.

30-Sep-2026

SQL Canvas Meets the Navigator — The SQL editor completes table and column names from your database, suggests joins, and hands a statement to the agent in one click.

29-Sep-2026

Celeris Provider — Celeris-1, a diffusion language model, is now available as an LLM provider.

28-Sep-2026

Several MCP Servers per Agent — One agent can read several data servers, such as two warehouses. Each call goes to the right server, and every step shows which one answered.

28-Sep-2026

Combine Results Across Sources — When an answer needs two systems, code joins their results and checks the join, and every combined figure traces back to each source.

28-Sep-2026

Ask Across Several Databases — Query PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, DuckDB and MongoDB in one conversation, read-only, with every statement checked in that database’s own dialect first.

23-Sep-2026

Every Number Has a Receipt — Figures are computed by code, not by the model’s own arithmetic. Click any marked number to see the exact rows it came from.

22-Sep-2026

The Living Answer — The answer streams in place without jumping. When it is done, a short receipt shows its steps and one verdict: Verified, N findings, or Not checked.

21-Sep-2026

One Clear Layout for Every Answer — The answer comes first. Notes, evidence and actions sit beneath it in the same layout every time, each one a click away.

20-Sep-2026

Talk to It While It Works — Send a note mid-answer and the agent uses it at its next step. Close the tab, come back, and the answer is still there.

20-Sep-2026

Regenerate as an Experiment — A second answer is scored beside the first, so you choose with a reason. Editing a question starts a branch, and nothing is overwritten.

20-Sep-2026

Recovery You Can Audit — When a model provider fails, a fallback model you approved takes over and the answer says so. Every recovery is recorded.

20-Sep-2026

Leaner Prompts, Tighter Turns — Repeated prompt content is cached and paid for once. Per agent, show the model only the tools it needs and give a turn a budget it can see.

20-Sep-2026

Also Available, Per Agent — Drafts can fix their own flagged issues, attachments can be read as verified sources, and you can watch what the ontology contributed, step by step.

19-Sep-2026

Wrong SQL Stopped Before It Runs — Queries are checked against your ontology before they run — wrong joins, missing columns, impossible values — and many are fixed automatically.

16-Sep-2026

A Primer That Folds Away — A session primer can collapse to two headers, so the conversation starts at your first real question.

12-Sep-2026

The Database Navigator — Browse any connected database as a living catalog: what each table is for, its keys, likely joins and masked previews, for you and for the agent.

12-Sep-2026

Ground an Agent on a Released Ontology — An agent can read only the published version of its knowledge graph, so work on the draft never changes its answers.

10-Sep-2026

Knowledge Graphs Searched by Meaning — A question about “customers” now finds an entity called Party. On by default.

07-Sep-2026

Subscriptions That Follow the Publisher — A subscribed agent pack brings its ontologies, skills and signatures, and updates in place when the publisher republishes.

05-Sep-2026

Ontologies Validated Against the Data — A knowledge graph can be checked against the real data when it is built, so the agent gets its queries right the first time.

28-Aug-2026

White-Label Branding — One server can present several branded products, each with its own name, look and email identity, chosen by web address.

17-Aug-2026

Progressive Disclosure Skills — A skill can be a whole library that the agent opens section by section, so deep expertise is on hand without being paid for on every turn.

16-Aug-2026

Signed Data Products — Declare a data product on your ontology and the platform proves its queries are safe before it can be signed. Every answer from it carries a verifiable receipt.

08-Aug-2026

Your Vote Now Teaches the Agent — A thumbs up or down now improves the part of the agent that produced the answer, and hovering a vote tells you what it will do.

07-Aug-2026

Trust, Open to Third Parties — Partners can add their own checks and controls to the Trust Circle. Each one arrives switched off and must be signed before use.

07-Aug-2026

The Trust Panel, Rebuilt — Trust settings are now the Trust Circle itself: pick a guarantee, see what protects it, and save everything with one button.

05-Aug-2026

Controls That Act Sooner — Repeated calls, runaway budgets and unsupported answers are now stopped during the turn, not just reported after it.

05-Aug-2026

One Home Per Measurement — Every quality score is counted once and grouped by the step it measures, so a protection doing its job never turns red because of a later score.

19-Jul-2026

One Design Language — Every panel shares one layout: key figures on top, a resizable divider and clear tabs below, with names that match the navigator.

19-Jul-2026

The Agent Anatomy — Configuration opens as the agent itself, drawn as a star. Click any part to land where it is configured.

19-Jul-2026

The Trust Circle — Eight live trust readings around every agent. Click a station to act on it, or press play to hear the agent’s story from its own records.

19-Jul-2026

From Finding to Chunk — A security finding in a document repository now points to the exact text that caused it, and can be exported as a report.

19-Jul-2026

Knowledge Answers, Grounded — Answers from your documents show they stayed inside them: unsupported claims are marked, and the agent says when the documents don’t cover a question.

19-Jul-2026

A Screened, Governed Knowledge Base — Every document is screened as it is added, a bad one is a click from quarantine, and answers show how fresh and trustworthy their sources are.

19-Jul-2026

Proven, Not Promised — The knowledge protections ship with a benchmark anyone can rerun for free, plus live attack tests that check the defenses actually held.

18-Jul-2026

Trust, Made Visible — See an agent’s data boundary on its knowledge graph, any drift across it in red, and each answer’s signed history as a chain you can verify.

16-Jul-2026

Test Your Own Defenses — Attack any agent with a live test set to see whether its guards held, then export a signed audit pack mapped to the EU AI Act, NIST and GDPR.

15-Jul-2026

Injection Firewalls — Hidden instructions in memories, documents and tool results are caught, closing the paths a check on your own question would miss.

13-Jul-2026

Human Review — A risky answer can be held for a person to approve, with nothing lost and nothing sent unseen. Ideal for unattended runs.

11-Jul-2026

Why Trust This Answer? — Every answer carries a plain-language trust summary and a signed record anyone can verify offline.

09-Jul-2026

Assurance Inbox & Policy Backtesting — Trust incidents land in one queue. Before tightening a policy, replay it over your history to see what it would have changed.

07-Jul-2026

Behavioral Trust Score — An agent’s trust follows its measured behavior, and a circuit breaker can alert you or pause it when behavior slips.

05-Jul-2026

The Trust Journey — Every answer shows, in one compact strip, which protections it passed and which of them acted.

03-Jul-2026

The Trust Membrane — A signed trust badge on every agent and shareable asset. An agent is trusted only if everything it is built from is, even after it is shared.

02-Jul-2026

Agent Authority — An agent working on its own can never exceed the authority you granted, and its actions are recorded as its own, not yours.

01-Jul-2026

Governed Metrics & Open Standards — Define a metric once and have the AI and your BI tools use it identically, then export it all in open W3C standards.

30-Jun-2026

Platform Ontology — A live map of your whole estate: every agent, what grounds it and what it uses, with one-click jumps to where each part is managed.

28-Jun-2026

Agent Memory — The agent remembers your preferences across sessions, per agent or shared, and you can view or erase every memory.

28-Jun-2026

Uderia as an MCP Server — Use any governed Uderia agent as a tool in Claude Desktop, Cursor or other agents, with every protection still applied.

27-Jun-2026

AI Guardrails — Personal data is masked, toxic output is blocked, and prompt injection is stopped before it reaches the model.

26-Jun-2026

Grounding Gate — Answers are checked against the agent’s declared data scope, and can be flagged or held when they drift outside it.

24-Jun-2026

Ontology — Turn Databricks industry data models into a knowledge graph, and deploy them as real Teradata databases with demo data.

21-Jun-2026

Agent Observation & Evaluation — Every turn and flow run is scored on quality, cost and safety, with a health view for each agent.

21-Jun-2026

Next Step Recommender — After each answer, one-tap suggestions for useful follow-up questions and actions, at little or no extra cost.

10-Jun-2026

Flow Parameters & Visual Debugging — Turn a flow into a reusable template, and debug it one node at a time while seeing each node’s input and output.

05-Jun-2026

Sharper Self-Learning — The agent learns only from turns that actually fetched data, so the approaches it reuses stay accurate.

17-May-2026

Dashboard Component — Pin any chart or table from the conversation to a persistent dashboard whose tiles refresh on demand.

16-May-2026

Visual Flow Orchestration — Describe a multi-step workflow and the agent builds and runs it as a live graph, with branches and parallel paths.

14-May-2026

New LLM Providers — MLX for Apple Silicon local inference and xAI for Grok models, expanding provider flexibility from hyperscalers to sovereign on-device execution.

12-May-2026

Scale Knowledge Graphs to Neo4j — Start on the built-in store and move large graphs to Neo4j, without changing agents or workflows.

10-May-2026

Infinity Context — The agent recalls the relevant parts of a long conversation instead of forgetting the oldest ones.

09-May-2026

Model Guide — Compare providers, models, context sizes and prices in the Uderia Model Guide, one click from the LLM settings.

03-May-2026

Your Workplace Apps, Connected — The agent works across Google, Microsoft 365 and Slack, with each user connecting their own accounts.

02-May-2026

Always-Fresh Knowledge — Knowledge repositories update themselves when source documents change, re-indexing only what is new.

02-May-2026

SAML 2.0 & JIT Provisioning — Connect to corporate identity providers via SAML 2.0; user roles update automatically at login based on IdP group membership.

01-May-2026

Task Scheduler — Schedule any agent query to run automatically on a cron or interval; manage schedules through conversation or the split-panel UI, with results delivered by email or webhook.

28-Apr-2026

Parallel Query Execution — Multi-step queries run faster: independent plan phases and date-range iterations now execute in parallel instead of sequentially.

16-Apr-2026

Knowledge Graphs in Agent Packs — Export and import Knowledge Graphs as part of agent packs; import restores graphs without displacing existing active graphs.

10-Apr-2026

Genie Coordinator Pass-Through — Single-expert queries skip the synthesis step, cutting coordinator token cost and response time in half.

04-Apr-2026

OpenRouter Support — Access 100+ models (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, and more) via a single API key.

15-Apr-2026

Teradata Hybrid Search — Enable BM25 hybrid search on Teradata VantageCloud knowledge repositories directly from the repository inspector.

Hybrid Search — Choose between semantic, hybrid (RRF), and keyword (BM25) search on Qdrant Cloud knowledge repositories.

08-Mar-2026

Teradata VantageCloud Backend — Store and search knowledge in Teradata VantageCloud with server-side embedding and enterprise-grade connection resilience.

ChromaDB & Qdrant Cloud — Zero-config local knowledge storage (ChromaDB) or managed cloud vector search (Qdrant), selectable per repository.

01-Mar-2026

Context Window Management — Control how much of your conversation history and knowledge the agent sees; configure per profile with live token budget visualization.

Canvas Component — Write and run SQL directly in the chat canvas with syntax highlighting and live result rendering.

27-Feb-2026

Data Visualization — Turn query results into interactive charts (16 types) automatically; the agent picks the right visual for your data.

23-Feb-2026

Extensions — Transform agent responses on the fly: extract JSON, classify, summarize, generate PDFs, or chain custom transformations with a single # trigger.

Skills - Pre-processing prompt injections with 5 built-in skills and visual editor

Dual-Model Cost Breakdown - Live Status displays strategic vs tactical costs for Fusion Optimizer dual-model executions with color-coded visualization

Theme-Aware Token/Cost KPIs - Live Status token and cost displays now adapt to both dark and light themes with consistent visibility

n8n Integration - Visual workflow automation with three production-ready templates (Simple Query, Scheduled Reports, Slack Integration) and comprehensive deployment guides

Agent Packs - Bundle complete agent teams (coordinator, experts, knowledge collections) into portable .agentpack files for one-click install, export, and marketplace sharing

Text to Speech - Voice output now available for all profile classes with Escape-to-cancel and smart text truncation

Agent Memory

Durable facts an agent remembers about you, recalled into every session. Unlike the Context Window (this session's working memory), there is nothing to configure here — Agent Memory is enabled per agent via the Agent Memory component and read/written in the Workspace panel.

Local memory

Remembered by one agent only. The default — facts an agent learns stay with that agent and never leak to your other agents.

Global memory

Shared across all of your agents. For genuine user-level facts every agent should know — your role, preferred units, answer style.

Each agent recalls its own Local memory  ∪  Global memory — deterministically ranked and injected every turn.

Knowledge Graph Retrieval

How a question finds the right entities in a bound ontology

When an agent is grounded on a knowledge graph, the question has to reach the right entities before anything else can go right. Matching the words the question used is precise but literal — it cannot connect “customers” to an entity called Party. Semantic matching adds a second channel that finds entities by meaning, so business vocabulary still reaches the deployed model. Word matches stay authoritative; meaning only widens what is considered.

Also find entities by meaning, not only by the words the question used. Each graph is embedded once and the result is cached on disk, so a restart re-loads it rather than rebuilding. A graph that has not been indexed yet answers from word matching alone while it builds in the background — a question is never delayed by it. Uses the embedding model configured above. (default: enabled)

Turn this off to match on words alone. Live Status reports which entities each turn reached by meaning, under Knowledge Graph Enrichment.

Trust

The deployment's assurance controls, in the order you set them up: measure, decide what counts as failing, decide what acts, decide what reaches you.

Scoring

Whether turns are measured at all, and whether LLM judges take part. PROVEN's receipts ride the same hook — sealing is on exactly when automatic scoring is.

Deterministically score every executed turn and flow run (free, non-blocking) and feed the Agent Performance roster. Turn off to score only on demand.

Add the LLM-judge panel to automatic scoring. Judges call an LLM (token cost), so they run only on a sampled fraction of turns plus all anomalous ones.

Fraction of turns also judged (1.0 = judge every turn). Anomalous turns are always judged when judges are on.

Quality bands

Where a check counts as healthy, worth a look, or a failure. Every measurement is counted at JUDGED, grouped by the moment of the turn it measures.
Preset:

Blast radius: these two floors colour every pass rate in the product — the Agent Roster bars, the Trust Circle's JUDGED reading, and the cross-agent KPI charts. The other seven stations report what their mechanisms did and are not coloured by a measurement, so these floors do not move them. Raising the green floor will turn currently-green agents amber immediately; it changes how quality is reported, never how a turn is scored or gated. Defaults 0.80 / 0.50. Only the numbers are configurable: whether a gate acts (enforce vs observe), and worst-of aggregation across agents, are properties of the system rather than judgements about where a bar sits.

Plan

Retrieve

Act

Compose

The run

Enforcement

Which controls may act on a turn. Each agent's own mode is set in the profile editor's Trust Configuration; these master switches govern the whole deployment.

Master switch for the grounding gate. When on, each profile's Grounding mode applies (default observe: surface KG scope drift without changing answers; annotate/enforce are opt-in per profile). Off → the gate never runs. The checks that GRADE this guarantee are tuned under JUDGED, with every other measurement — a threshold tunes a measurement, and measurement is counted in one place.

Master switch for the deterministic guardrail. When on, each profile's Guardrail mode applies (default observe: detect outbound PII & toxicity without changing answers; annotate/enforce — PII redaction, toxicity withhold — are opt-in per profile). 0-token. Off → the guardrail never runs.

The ONE aggregate: fuses each agent's Trust-Membrane integrity (signed / changed / unsigned) with its live conduct — a recency-weighted blend of the trust-critical checks with every remaining check, each dimension counted exactly once — into one composite state (Provisional / At-risk / Watch / Proven / Trusted). Integrity can only cap conduct, never promote it. Read-side only: never gates a turn; surfaces the seal+ring on the Agents roster and the Trust Posture matrix. Off → the ring is hidden.

Trips only on the volume-gated transition into At-risk (one alert per bad streak). Freeze touches unattended use only (Agent Authority autonomous=false + frozen_by_breaker) — interactive use is never affected; visible and reversible in the Agent Authority card. Incidents land in the Assurance Inbox (Agents view).

{% include "enterprise/obda_policy.html" ignore missing %}

Assessment modules

Which module assesses each property, during the turn and after it. One assessment, up to two lanes — changing a row moves both the gate's input and the score, together. Each change is applied and audited on its own.

Third-party modules

Packs may add properties and ways of assessing them. They never add a station, an enforcement act, or a binding — and installing one assigns nothing: you bind it above, and that is audited. A pack must be signed before it can be bound.

What reaches you

Each station's reporting level. Danger always surfaces — this filters what is presented in the Assurance Inbox, the badge and the ring, never what is recorded.
SIGNED born, then attested
GROUNDED truth · faithfulness
GUARDED rules · safety
BOUNDED authority, borrowed
JUDGED execution quality, graded
TRUSTED the badge breathes
REVIEWED a human decides
PROVEN receipts, not promises

Prompt Cache

                                            
Pay for the stable prefix once; a miss on an unchanged prefix is a finding

                                        

                                    

                                    
                                
                                

                                    
The provider's prompt cache serves the system prompt and the conversation so far — the part of every call that does not change — at its cached rate. It changes nothing about what the agent says; only what the prefix costs. Governed by the deployment's prompt-caching switch.

                                    

                                        

                                            Use the provider's prompt cache
                                            
Explicit breakpoints where the provider has them (Anthropic — natively or behind OpenRouter); order-only elsewhere (OpenAI, Gemini); no effect on providers without a cache.

                                        

                                        
                                    

                                    

                                        

                                            Cache lifetime
                                            
How long the cached prefix stays warm between calls. One hour costs more to write and suits a long working session.

                                Trust
                            

                            
The agent’s posture, grouped by Trust Circle station — what it may reference, claim, emit and do unattended

                        


                        
                        

                            
                            

                                
                                    

                                        
                                        

                                            
Agent posture

                                            
One hardening intent — every gate below follows it unless it overrides

                                        

                                    

                                    
                                
                                

                                    

                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                    

                                    
                                    

                                    
Each gate below defaults to Inherit. A gate set to an explicit mode overrides this default for its surface only — the summary above always shows what actually applies.

                                

                            

                        


                        
                        

                            
Grounded — truth · faithfulness

                        

                        
                        

                            

                                
                                    

                                        
                                        

                                            
Grounding

                                            
Keep answers within the declared scope

                                        

                                    

                                    
                                
                                

                                    
                                    

                                        
Knowledge graph

                                        
May the answer reference data outside the graph's declared scope?

                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                    

                                    
                                    

                                        
Knowledge repository

                                        
Are the answer's claims supported by the retrieved documents?

                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                    

                                    
Requires the admin Grounding Enforcement master switch (Administration → Config → Trust → Enforcement). Thresholds are shared from there. A segment without its source — no graph bound, or nothing retrieved — abstains cleanly.

                                

                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                
                                    

                                        
                                        

                                            
Honesty

                                            
Stop a failed retrieval being reported as a confirmed “there is none”

                                        

                                    

                                    
                                
                                

                                    

                                        
Honesty mode

                                        
Fires only when the answer asserts non-existence and every data query that turn failed — or, for knowledge agents, when retrieval ran and found (near-)nothing yet the answer asserts specifics. A legitimate empty result is never altered.

                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                    

                                    

                                        
Grain substitution

                                        
A second honesty check: a question answered at a coarser grain than it asked (“which customer” answered by state) gets a disclosure appended — the figure itself is correct governed data and is never replaced. The detection is deterministic (0 tokens); the optional judge below confirms the heuristic before it acts.

                                        
                                    

                                    
Deterministic, 0-token. Abstains cleanly on turns with no failed data queries and no retrieval, so chat turns are never flagged.

                                

                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                
                                    

                                        
                                        

                                            
Outcome Loop

                                            
Revise a draft that fails the grounding check once, before delivery — the gate is the rubric

                                        

                                    

                                    
                                
                                

                                    

                                        
When the grounding check finds something the model can fix — an unsupported claim, a reference outside the declared scope, a figure that matches no result — the draft gets one revision with the finding named, and the same check grades the revision. A revision that clears is delivered clean; one that does not delivers the honest annotated first draft — never a second silent try. Both drafts are kept and sealed.

                                        
Off = today's behaviour. The grader is exact and costs nothing; the revision is one LLM call, shown in Live Status with its cost. Requires the deployment master switch. Posture — part of the agent's signature.

                                    

                                    
                                    

                                        

                                            
                                            
                                            
Each revision is one LLM call.

                                        

                                        

                                            Revisable findings
                                            
                                            
                                            
                                        

                                    

                                

                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                
                                    

                                        
                                        

                                            
Attachment Sources

                                            
What the platform reads from an attached image, PDF, CSV or text — and vouches for

                                        

                                    

                                    
                                
                                

                                    

                                        
An attachment the platform can read itself — a table OCR'd from a screenshot, a PDF's tables and text, a CSV, a text file — becomes a verified source: the grounding check holds the answer to it, the compute tool can operate on its rows, and a figure quoted from it traces to the file and its region. Deterministic, no model involved.

                                        
Always on for this agent when the deployment master switch is on. The one option below adds an unverified reading for an image nothing could read.

                                    

                                    
                                

                            

                        



                        
                        

                            
Guarded — rules · safety

                        

                        
                        

                            

                                
                                    

                                        
                                        

                                            
Guardrails

                                            
Detect & redact outbound PII and block toxic content

                                        

                                    

                                    
                                
                                

                                    

                                        
Outbound guardrail mode

                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                    

                                    

                                        

                                            Check PII
                                            
Email, SSN, credit card, phone, API keys, IBAN, IP.

                                        

                                        
                                    

                                    

                                        

                                            Check toxicity
                                            
Threat / violence / self-harm / weapon markers (heuristic).

                                        

                                        
                                    

                                    

                                        
Inbound guardrail mode (prompt-injection on incoming requests)

                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                    

                                    
Requires the admin Guardrails (P2) master switch (Administration → Config → Trust → Enforcement). Deterministic, 0-token. Findings carry category labels only — never the raw value.

                                

                            

                        



                        
                        

                            
Bounded — authority, borrowed

                        

                        
                        

                            

                                
                                    

                                        
                                        

                                            
Agent Authority

                                            
Scope what this agent may do when it acts on its own — its identity is the Profile itself

                                        

                                    

                                    
                                
                                

                                    

                                        
When this agent runs autonomously — a Coordinate expert, a scheduled task, a flow node, or an MCP call — it acts as a scoped identity derived from you. Every autonomous action is attributed to the agent in the audit trail.

                                        
Leave everything untouched to inherit your full authority — the agent behaves exactly as today. A scope only ever removes permissions, never adds them.

                                    

                                    

                                        

                                            Allow autonomous action
                                            
Off → this agent may not act on its own at all (interactive use is unaffected).

                                        

                                        
                                    

                                    

                                        

                                            Read-only (block writes)
                                            
Deny any tool that writes, inserts, updates, deletes, or sends.

                                        

                                        
                                    

                                    

                                        
                                        
                                        
Comma-separated tool names this agent may never call. Blank = no per-tool block.

                                    

                                    

                                        
                                        
                                        
If set, restrict platform connectors to only these. Blank = all connectors allowed.

                                    

                                    

                                        
                                        
                                        
Cap the cost of a single autonomous run. Blank = no cap.

                                    

                                    

                                        
                                        
                                        
Four eyes: the accounts (usernames, comma-separated) that decide the writes this agent parks for review. When set, only they can approve or reject — you, the owner, cannot. Blank = you decide. Every name must be an active account other than yours, or nothing is saved.

                                    

                                    

                                        
                                        
How this agent participates in OBDA-READ (requires the OBDA-READ component to be enabled for it).

                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
                                        
The signed data products this agent may consume (comma-separated). Both options above require at least one — an empty list saves as “Disable”.

                                    

                                    

                                        
                                        

                                            
                                            
By default everything above applies only when the agent runs unattended (scheduled, in a flow, as an expert, or over MCP) — on the reasoning that a present human is the control. Turn this on and the agent's authority is its authority whoever started the turn, so "surface-only" confines your own chat as well. Off = unchanged.

                                        

                                    

                                    

                                        
                                        
When this agent cannot go on without a person — two of your things share a name, a step needs a value it was not given, a data source asks — it stops and asks instead of guessing. How it asks is authority: unsigned, and weakening it is a recorded downgrade.

                                        

                                            

                                                
                                                
                                            

                                            

                                                
                                                
                                            

                                            

                                                
                                                
                                            

                                            

                                                
                                                
                                            

                                        

                                        
                                        
                                        
One per line, key = value. Written here or by answering a question with “remember for this agent”. A standing answer is used instead of asking, and its use is recorded on the turn. A deployment held at observe by its administrator overrides the platform-question setting.

                                    

                                    
Enforced fail-closed at every tool chokepoint. Framework reporting tools (TDA_*) are always permitted; a surface-only agent's compiled product statements are the one raw-SQL exception, registered per turn by the surface itself.

                                

                            

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                
                                    

                                        
                                        

                                            
Turn Budget

                                            
How much one turn may spend — the model sees what is left, and finishes gracefully when it runs out

                                        

                                    

                                    
                                
                                

                                    

                                        
A budget is visible to the model: at every tool boundary it reads how many steps, tokens and seconds are left. When a unit runs out the next tool call is refused (naming what is left) and the answer is written from what was collected — a recorded graceful finish, never a silent kill. The Live Status header shows the bar; the dock offers Continue where it stopped.

                                        
Leave every unit blank for no budget — the agent behaves exactly as today. Each unit is optional; the hard stops (per-run cost cap, context limit) stay the last line above it. Requires the deployment master switch. A raised ceiling is a posture change and re-signs the agent.

                                    

                                    

                                        

                                            
                                            
                                            
Data-tool calls per turn (framework tools never count).

                                        

                                        

                                            
                                            
                                            
Input + output tokens across the turn's LLM calls.

                                        

                                        

                                            
                                            
                                            
Wall-clock from the turn's start.

                                        

                                    

                                

                            

                        



                        
                        

                            
Judged — execution quality, graded

                        


                        
                        

                            

                                
                                    

                                        
                                        

                                            
Judges

                                            
LLM judges grade this agent’s delivered answers — a confirmed failure files in the Assurance Inbox

                                        

                                    

                                    
                                
                                

                                    

                                        
Judge this agent’s turns

                                        
                                        
                                        
                                    

                                    

                                        
                                        
Fraction of this agent’s turns the judges grade (anomalous turns are always judged). Empty = platform default. 1.0 = every turn — for a high-stakes agent.

                                        
                                    

                                    

                                        

                                            File condemnations in the Assurance Inbox
                                            
A delivered answer a judge convicts of being ungrounded becomes a danger incident you can acknowledge — the feedback loop, not just a number on a card.

                                        

                                        
                                    

                                    
Requires the platform scoring master (Automatic Agent Scoring). Judged turns render on the Quality card with the ·judge tag and feed the JUDGED station.

                                

                            

                        


                        
                        
REVIEWED is armed above, not here: set any gate to Review and withheld work parks in the Assurance Inbox for your decision. SIGNED is an act (the trust seal on the profile card), TRUSTED and PROVEN are aggregates the platform computes — nothing to configure per profile.
